reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a tutorial about transferring virtual GTA Online cash between player accounts. The described process uses a percentage of cash from a recent in-game job, and the gameplay frame shows an in-game cash balance rather than an external payment flow. The request to like and subscribe is ordinary audience engagement, not a condition for receiving money.

citations.quote: How to give money to other players in gta 5 online
today I'm gonna be telling you guys on how to transfer money from your account. Whether it be your main account or a second account to another GC Online player.
you can see how much money you. Can actually share which is for me $1,022 and then all you do is give a percentage.
This can only be obtained from new jobs, new free room events or any other way.

opening.argument: The presentation combines an easy-money premise with direct audience acquisition. It advertises giving money to other players, tells viewers to like and subscribe, and points them to a channel, Twitter, and Twitch. Even though it does not expressly say that subscribing unlocks the transfer, the reward-focused tutorial and the engagement and external-contact prompts appear together, creating a solicitation pathway around obtaining in-game cash. The money is presented as easy to generate and share after a job, which can encourage viewers to follow the creator's requested actions in pursuit of that outcome.

citations.quote: How to give money to other players in gta 5 online
Be sure you do leave a like and subscribe
DONT CLICK THIS ~ https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCKy8iL7wIDZ7ZGFhqXsx3qQ?sub_confirmation=1 Twitter: https://twitter.com/why_not_gta Twitch : https://www.twitch.tv/whynotgta_yt
if you actually do a job, you get like 20 grand from that job,. And you can actually give it to your friend

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the links ordinary engagement does not resolve the surrounding solicitation. The description uses a subscription link while the video promotes obtaining and transferring cash, and the presenter repeatedly directs viewers to subscribe and visit other channels. The tutorial may describe game mechanics, but the relevant concern is that the attractive reward topic is used to draw viewers toward the creator's requested actions.

citations.quote: DONT CLICK THIS ~ https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCKy8iL7wIDZ7ZGFhqXsx3qQ?sub_confirmation=1
go check out some other videos because they are all quite helpful

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material shows promotion, but it does not establish that liking, subscribing, or visiting a link is required to receive money. The transfer is described as an in-game percentage from a qualifying job, not as a reward granted for an audience action. The alleged linkage is inferred rather than shown.

citations.quote: you can see how much money you. Can actually share which is for me $1,022 and then all you do is give a percentage
This can only be obtained from new jobs, new free room events or any other way.

opening.argument: Several genuine warning signals appear together: the description says “DONT CLICK THIS” while supplying a subscription URL and multiple external social links; the video discusses transferring money between accounts; and it advertises a low-effort route to substantial game earnings, including “like 20 grand” from a job. The presenter also admits uncertainty about the applicable cap and says some jobs do not work. That combination of an attractive cash outcome, unclear limits, and external directions makes the offer unusually difficult for a viewer to verify and supports treating it as deceptive reward acquisition.

citations.quote: DONT CLICK THIS ~ https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCKy8iL7wIDZ7ZGFhqXsx3qQ?sub_confirmation=1 Twitter: https://twitter.com/why_not_gta Twitch : https://www.twitch.tv/whynotgta_yt
As of right now, I do not know what the cap is.
just made it so some jobs don't work
if you actually do a job, you get like 20 grand from that job

rebuttal.rebuttal: The gameplay setting does not eliminate the red flags. The description still combines an imperative-style warning with a subscription URL and social contacts, while the narration presents a cash-transfer method whose limits and reliability are uncertain. A disclaimer that some jobs fail can make the pitch seem candid without proving that the promised outcome is dependable.

citations.quote: DONT CLICK THIS ~ https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCKy8iL7wIDZ7ZGFhqXsx3qQ?sub_confirmation=1
As of right now, I do not know what the cap is.
just made it so some jobs don't work

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals show uncertainty and ordinary self-promotion, not a deceptive claim. The speaker expressly limits the method: existing account money cannot be used, races fail, and the amount is only a percentage of qualifying job cash. The evidence therefore describes constraints rather than an external reward or guaranteed return.

citations.quote: This can only be obtained from new jobs, new free room events or any other way.
Races that didn't work and you any money you win from races apparently you can't transfer
it's not a lot of money at the end of the day

opening.argument: Although packaged as instruction, the video functions as promotion for participation in a money-acquisition method and for the creator's channels. It opens with repeated like-and-subscribe requests, calls the other videos “quite helpful,” directs viewers to Twitter and other videos, and presents the method as working after the creator's testing. The operational details make the pitch credible, while the title foregrounds giving money to players. That instructional framing can steer viewers toward the creator's ecosystem and toward trying an easy in-game cash pathway.

citations.quote: Be sure you do leave a like and subscribe
go check out some other videos because they are all quite helpful
But no it does work
How to give money to other players in gta 5 online

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructional packaging is precisely what makes the promotion persuasive: the creator presents personal testing, explains which jobs fail, then concludes that the method works and directs viewers to more content. Calling this merely education overlooks the repeated channel-building requests and the attractive cash-transfer subject used to retain attention and encourage participation.

citations.quote: i spent a considerable amount of time on races to see if
But no it does work
go check out some other videos because they are all quite helpful

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a channel does not turn an operational game tutorial into a scam. The method is explained with concrete restrictions, including that the money must come from a new job or event and that the recipient receives only a selected percentage. Nothing here shows payment, registration, or a promised real-world reward for viewers.
